bodies.thread:
Most personal finance tools start by categorizing transactions, but that is the wrong first step. A statement either reconciles to the paisa or it does not.

Moneytrail rejects scanned PDFs rather than guessing at them. It uses a reconciliation gate to verify arithmetic against bank-published data before categorizing anything.

The codebase uses no floats to represent money because binary floating-point math cannot promise accuracy to the paisa. Amounts are written as exact decimals.

A test of 225 transactions across three months of an HDFC statement reconciled to the paisa against the bank's summary block.

Merchant coverage on a real 225-transaction statement was 18%. Chasing that number would be the wrong response.

Language models can produce a confident, plausible, but incorrect number when asked to read a ledger. The system validates model-generated JSON into a Query object to prevent the model from inventing merchants.

Personal finance tools must prioritize a reconciliation gate over categorization to ensure data integrity, as silent parsing errors render subsequent financial insights unreliable.
